metadata.case_name: SUEN KAM WAI v. CHEUNG YAM

plaintiff.occupation_after: Welder (returned to former employment with Kwong Ngai Steel Works)

injuries.description: Right kidney lacerated beyond repair; nephrectomy performed.
source: The right kidney was found to be lacerated beyond repair and nephrectomy was done.

injuries.description: Adhesion over the intra-abdominal organs resulting from the operation which could give rise to an operation within the next 10-20 years (chance around 10%).
source: He also stated that the adhesion over the intra-abdominal organs resulting from the operation could give rise to an operation some time within the next 10-20 years. He put the chance of such an operation eventuating at around 10%.

manifestations.description: Renal function tests revealing marginal impairment
Finds work much more tiring; leaves much more tired and sleepy at the end of the working day

treatments_received: Out-patient clinic attendances during convalescence and after return to work
treatments_future: Possible operation for intra-abdominal adhesions (chance around 10% within 10-20 years)

losses.description: Loss of the right kidney (nephrectomy) with resulting marginal impairment of renal function and increased fatigue, and the possibility of future surgery for intra-abdominal adhesions.

comparable_cases.case_name: Chan Chuen v Cheng Ka Kui and Chow Keung Kwong v Cheng Ka Kui
comparable_cases.injury_description: In that case Mr Chow lost a kidney and the spleen.
